title: State Subsidies Subside Further
text:
State Subsidies Subside Further

Thomas Gatley

Gavekal Dragonomics | 5 Aug 2026

The political backlash in the US and Europe against trade with China often focuses on manufacturing subsidies and industrial-policy support, which are alleged to cause unfair competition and excess capacity (see Europe’s China Shock In Perspective). For its part, Beijing denies that there is any systemic overcapacity, but says it is cracking down on illegal subsidies by local governments as part of its campaign to prevent wasteful investment and destructive competition (see Course Corrections Into 2026).What’s the reality behind this conflicting rhetoric? The financial reports of listed companies show that the support most likely to come from local governments has declined significantly since 2022, a casualty of tight budgets and changing political priorities. The remaining benefits are still sizable, but are more driven by central-government policies and are unlikely to shrink dramatically. The main channel of Chinese industrial policy is no longer tax benefits or direct subsidies from the government budget, but privileged access to equity capital. And equity financing for favored sectors, particularly semiconductors, is picking up again.
